3.  Professional Services Agreement for On-Call Planning Consultant
  Due to anticipated increased volume in high level planning items, including multiple large
  scale housing developments, potential hospital construction, and significant potential
  legislative changes to the Transient Rental License Ordinance, City staff recommend
  increasing the maximum potential contract with Sagecrest by 20% to $150,000 during the
  next one year renewal period.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to renew the professional services agreement
  with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC for on-call Planning Consultant services
  for an additional one year term for an annual cumulative total not to exceed $1 50,000.00.

4.  Declare Vehicles and Equipment as Surplus
  Historically, the City Council is presented with a list of items that are surplus, the Council
  declares it surplus, and then the declared items are either sold via Public Surplus, given
  to charity, or disposed of properly. Staff has compiled a list of vehicles that the City of
  Avalon (City”) no longer uses and is insufficient for the current needs.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution declaring vehicles and equipment listed in resolution as surplus
  property and authorize the City Manager to dispose of it in accordance with City policy.

5.  Adoption of an Ordinance Amending Title 4, Chapter 4, Article 17 Vehicle Registration
  On January 30, 2024 City Council introduced and waived all readings of an ordinance to
  require the marking of certain vehicles due to the increase in applications and approvals

  for commercial autoettes, commercial rental autoettes, interior commercial vehicles, and
  public service/public health and safety vehicles.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt an ordinance of the City of Avalon amending Title 4, Chapter 4, Article 17 adding
  the requirement to mark all commercial autoettes, commercial rental autoettes,
  commercial vehicles, interior commercial vehicles, and public service/public health and
  safety vehicles with the legal name or fictitious business name of the applicant.

GENERAL BUSINESS

6.  Authorization to Purchase Parts and Materials from Shields, Harper & Company for the
  Underground Fuel Tank Replacement Project.
  California requires the owners or operators of specific types of underground fuel storage
  tanks to permanently close by December 31, 2025. The City of Avalon owns four
  underground fuel tanks at the Avalon Fuel Dock that fall under this requirement.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager, or their designee, to purchase parts and materials from
  Shields, Harper & Company, at a cost not to exceed $35,000, for the Underground Fuel
  Tank Replacement project.

7.  Authorize PERC to Purchase Spare Pump for Catherine Saltwater Booster Station
  PERC Water maintains the City’s Wastewater Treatment Plant, which includes the
  Catherine Saltwater Booster Station. This booster station supplies all of the saltwater for
  Avalon, and is vital part to our City’s saltwater infrastructure. Having a spare pump readily
  available ensures a swift response to pump failures. Quick replacement of a
  malfunctioning pump minimizes downtime and helps maintain the continuous and efficient
  operation of the booster station.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize PERC to purchase a Weinman pump from California Electric Motor Source
  (CEMS) to be used as a spare pump for the Catherine Saltwater Booster Station.
  Allocate funds from Saltwater Fund 11 3256552 for the procurement in the amount of
  not to exceed $36,000.

ADJOURN

Devin Elise Hart, Management Analyst

SUBJECT:  Professional Services Agreement for On-Call Planning Consultant

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager or his designee to renew the
professional services agreement with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC for on-call
Planning Consultant services for an additional one year term for an annual cumulative total not
to exceed $150,000.00.

REPORT SUMMARY: On March 21, 2023 the City Council authorized the City Manager to
execute a professional services agreement with Sagecrest Planning and Environmental, LLC
(‘Sagecrest”) for on-call planning consultant services for a not to exceed contract sum of
$125,000.

Prior to City Council authorization, the City of Avalon had been seeking technical planning and
environmental review expertise through advertising for a full-time Planning Director position.
However, though a job posting for a vacant Planning Director position had been advertised an
approximate 10 month period, from May 2022 to March 2023, the City had not been able to
identify a suitable candidate.

The agreement with Sagecrest allows the City to utilize a broad range of consultants with
expertise in varying areas of planning, development and land use entitlements.

During Sagecrest’s 10-month tenure as the City’s on-call planning consultant, they have
provided significant assistance to staff regarding a myriad of planning and environmental items
including, but not limited to:
  -  Processing of planning entitlement applications, including Conditional Use Permits,
  Tentative Parcel Maps, Site Plan Reviews, and Coastal Development Permits;
  -  Restarting the Local Coastal Program amendment process to address seal level rise and
  climate change planning;
  -  Meeting with prospective planning entitlement/building permit applicants to answer
  planning questions in person, via email and phone;
  -  Regularly reviewing legislation to keep the City up to date on State planning regulations;
  -  Preparing multiple municipal code updates to fulfill the requirements of the reporting for
  the Housing Element Implementation Plan;
  -  Preparing the 2023 General Plan and Housing Element annual reports, due April 1;
  -  Coordinating with City staff on research into potential updates to the City’s Transient
  Rental Licensing program;
   -  Continuously meeting and conferring with Island Stakeholders regarding potential
  development and land use including, Catalina Island Health.

During 8 months of the contract period, the City has expended approximately $82,500 for
planning services with Sagecrest. It is anticipated the 12-month contract will be less than
$125,000. The cost for services provided by Sagecrest compared to the potential cost of a fully
weighted full-time Planning Director salary ($180,000) results in a significant cost savings to the
City. Additionally, due to Sagecrest’s experience in the field, the City has experienced a
significant cost savings (more than $55,000) in planning related legal fees in 2023 compared to
2022.

Due to anticipated increased volume in high level planning items, including multiple large scale
housing developments, potential hospital construction, and significant potential legislative
changes to the Transient Rental License Ordinance, City staff recommend increasing the
maximum potential contract with Sagecrest by 20% to $150,000 during the next one year
renewal period.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Sustainability of operations.

FISCAL IMPACTS: FY 2023-24 Planning Services budget has contract sum budgeted (account
number 10255-5055).

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will not have
specialized planning support.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager, or their designee, to purchase
parts and materials from Shields, Harper & Company, at a cost not to exceed $35,000, for
the Underground Fuel Tank Replacement project.

REPORT SUMMARY: The State of California requires the owners or operators of specific types
of underground fuel storage tanks to permanently close by December 31, 2025. The City of
Avalon owns four underground fuel tanks at the Avalon Fuel Dock that fall under this
requirement.

With assistance from former Assemblymember Patrick O’Donnell, the City was awarded a
$500,000 State budget earmark that is administered through the State of California Water Board
to remove the underground fuel tanks located at the fuel dock and install an above ground
system in compliance with the new regulations. The granting agreement requires the City to
complete the project by February 29, 2024.

The total cost of the proposed materials acquisition is estimated to be 34,022.68. The not to
exceed amount of $35,000 will allow us to include the barge fees. The project associated with
these materials is included in the FY22-23 Budget and Capital Improvement Plan Project  —

Number 207004, Account Number 11470-6547 with $700,000 budgeted.
  —

Shields, Harper & Company is located in Orange, CA, and has a proven track record of
providing high-quality parts and materials for similar projects. Their products meet or exceed
industry standards, ensuring the longevity and reliability of the new fuel storage system. Their
combination of high-quality products, competitive pricing, experience, and reliability makes
them the most advantageous choice for the City.
It is recommended that the City Council approve the purchase of parts and materials from
Shields, Harper & Company for the Underground Fuel Tank Replacement Project. They are
the only supplier of this type that can offer the complete list of materials needed for the project.
Obtaining quotes from other suppliers would require a tremendous amount to staff time due to
the variety of materials needed from numerous different sources. The cost comparison would
not be apples to apples comparability with this current quote from Shields, Harbor & Company
because of the multiple suppliers. Procuring these materials from Shields, Harper & Company
is considered the best competitive value, and fulfills the purchasing procedure requirement
specified in the Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4.106(c).

207004 (account 11470-6547).

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize PERC to purchase a Weinman pump from
California Electric Motor Source (CEMS) to be used as a spare pump for the Catherine
Saltwater Booster Station. Allocate funds from Saltwater Fund 11325-6552 for the
procurement in the amount of not to exceed $36,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: PERC Water maintains the City’s Wastewater Treatment Plant, which
includes the Catherine Saltwater Booster Station. This booster station supplies all of the
saltwater for Avalon, and is vital part to our City’s saltwater infrastructure. Having a spare pump
readily available ensures a swift response to pump failures. Quick replacement of a
malfunctioning pump minimizes downtime and helps maintain the continuous and efficient
operation of the booster station.

The Catherine Saltwater Booster Station has two pumps, and normally runs on one pump.
Once a pump is removed for maintenance it will take at least three weeks for it to be returned
after service at the vendor on the mainland. For this reason the Director of Public Works and
the WWTP Facilities Manager determined that a backup pump is necessary to have in our
inventory ready for immediate installation to reduce the high risk pf a pump being off the island
for an extended duration for repair. Under this scenario, the redundant pump is replaced at the
booster station, and the failed pump is sent over for service and then placed into inventory once
it returns.

Quotes were obtained from California Electric Motor Source (CEMS), and Manufacturers
Edge. These were the only two pump suppliers that were able to offer a pump with the
specifications required for the needs of the Catherine Saltwater Booster Station. This fulfills
the purchasing procedure requirements under AMC Section 3-4.106 (a). Staff is requesting
authority to purchase the pump for a not to exceed cost of $36,000 to cover PERC markup,
and barge fee’s.
